subject: URGENT: edge degradation & request to evacuate traffic from us-west-2-a
messages:
From: Derek Santos <derek.santos@blueharbor.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-07 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2-a — can you force traffic away?

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a latency and 5xx surge from your edge in us-west-2-a around 08:45 PT. Our customers are experiencing timeouts on the API calls that hit Redwood, and overall p50 has jumped from 120ms to ~2.4s with 10-12% 5xx tail on generate endpoints. We've attached a small traffic snapshot and some sample request IDs.

Can you advise whether you can steer traffic away from us-west-2-a for BlueHarbor while you investigate? We need a short-term evacuation option — our app degrades severely when those tokens fail.

We've already throttled some features but would prefer Redwood do routing at the platform level so we don't have to implement app-side retries.

Thanks — happy to jump on a bridge.

Derek Santos
SRE Lead, BlueHarbor Logistics
ops@blueharbor.com

Attachments: edge-request-traffic-snapshot-1129.log (text), sample-reqids.txt (text)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-07 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2-a — can you force traffic away?

Derek — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We see the same telemetry on our side: influx of KV cache pressure plus a spike in GPU OOM-retries on a small subset of model variants pinned to that AZ.

Immediate actions we can take now:
- Force steering policy for BlueHarbor to prefer us-west-2-b / us-west-1 for 30 minutes (rollbackable)
- Throttle batch size for the affected model variants (short-term quality tradeoff)
- Open an incident bridge and run a focused kernel/memory sweep on the nodes in us-west-2-a

If you're ok with a platform-level traffic evacuation, I'll coordinate with Hannah to put the policy in place and notify you when traffic is moving. Will also attach a quick evacuation plan.

I'll kick off an incident bridge at 09:30 PT unless you ask for earlier.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Logan / Team —

I've validated the telemetry: nodes in us-west-2-a are showing elevated GPU swap and kernel retry counts for model family rdx-turbo-v1. There are also a handful of healthcheck timeouts from the autoscaler. My recommendation: execute a soft-evacuation (drain) for BlueHarbor's traffic with these constraints:

- Target: divert 95% of BlueHarbor sessions off us-west-2-a to us-west-2-b and us-west-1 over 10 minutes (ramp 30/70).
- Keep 5% pinned as a canary to monitor rollback safety.
- Apply batching cap reduction to 8 tokens per batch for affected route to reduce memory pressure.
- Instrument an SLO delta metric and watch p999 for 20 minutes before completing.

I'll prepare the evacuation policy in the console and put an autoscaler hold on the suspect pool so we don't trigger flapping. Attaching the proposed-evacuation-plan-v1.pdf.

Hannah
Director, Regional Reliability

Subject: Re: sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2-a — mitigation complete and next steps

Derek / BlueHarbor team —

Short update following the bridge and evacuation we ran earlier today. Summary:

- At 17:02 PT we initiated the soft-evacuation policy for BlueHarbor; by 17:09 PT 95% of sessions were rerouted to us-west-2-b (30%) and us-west-1 (65%). 5% stayed in us-west-2-a as a canary.
- Latency stabilized: p50 returned to ~130ms and 5xx rate dropped from 11% -> 0.6% within 12 minutes.
- Root cause appears to be a model-variant memory regression caused by a recent kernel switch during a behind-the-scenes kernel optimizer rollout (affects rdx-turbo-v1-quant). We've rolled that kernel back on the impacted pool and applied a kernel pin for BlueHarbor routes.
- We've attached the evacuation snapshot and the plan we executed.

Next steps / ask from BlueHarbor:
1) Please confirm you see the same improvement on your end and whether you want us to keep the traffic steering in place for another 24 hours (recommended) or return to normal routing.
2) We'll run a controlled test tomorrow morning to validate no regression on us-west-2-b before fully rolling the kernel change back globally.
3) Our CS team will prepare a credit proposal if you request commercial remediation — Marissa is looped for that.

If you want us to keep the steering for an extra 24 hours, reply "KEEP-STEER" and we'll extend the policy. If you'd like traffic returned immediately, reply "ROLLBACK-STEER" and we'll begin a 10-minute ramp back.

Thanks for the patience and for the sample logs — those helped isolate the regression quickly.

— Logan Wright
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
